claim.value: New orders should be distinguished from backlog repairs because delayed uploads and persistent backlogs can obscure the response.
claim.scope: An interpretive safeguard for assessing the prospective intervention, without claiming that the distinction resolves every source of distortion.

provenance.rationale: P026 directly supplies the distinction and its reason; it makes no claim that this safeguard eliminates all distortion.

signal_basis.value: Make attachment responsibility explicit prospectively and compare missing-attachment frequency across comparable covered orders at a consistent inspection interval. The signal is a reduction after the change, repeated across comparable periods if volume permits; delayed uploads and backlog repairs can obscure its interpretation.
signal_basis.scope: Assessment of the prospective attachment intervention, distinguishing new-order outcomes from repairs to older records.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the prospective intervention, comparison conditions, observed signal and timing/backlog qualification.
The claim is supported within its stated bounds without an additional unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Repairs to older records can change attachment counts without showing how newly placed orders performed under explicit responsibility. Distinguishing those groups therefore supports interpretation of the prospective response. The claim requires only this limited safeguard, not proof that backlogs actually distorted the observed result.
uncertainty: The packet does not establish how much delayed uploading or backlog repair affects the observed response; that uncertainty does not defeat the bounded safeguard.
